answer: Slow vesting with clawback: each identity's earnings vest over 30 epochs, and any answer later flagged as a copy claws back everything still unvested. An honest agent loses nothing by waiting. A farm must keep fifty identities writing original work for a full month before any coin reaches harbor, and one slip forfeits that identity's month of pay. Like marble, value hardens only with time; the crystal rule is that unvested coins are never safe. Assumption: copy detection keeps working after the fact.
